items.readable_text:
Content:
The general formula for the [MATH: n]th term of a geometric sequence is
[MATH: a_n = a_1 \cdot r^{n-1},]

Content:
where [MATH: a_1] is the first term and [MATH: r] is the common ratio.

Content:
To illustrate how this works, suppose we want to find the [MATH: 10]th term of the following geometric sequence:

Content:
[MATH: 3, \: 6, \: 12, \: \ldots]

Content:
The first term is [MATH: a_1=3,] and the common ratio is [MATH: r=2,] so we can write the formula for the [MATH: n]th term of the sequence:

Content:
[MATH: a_{n}|= a_{1} ⋅ r^{n − 1}; = 3 ⋅ 2^{n − 1}]

Content:
To find the [MATH: 10]th term, we can use this formula with [MATH: n={\color{blue}10}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: a_{n}|= 3 ⋅ 2^{n − 1}; a_{10}|= 3 ⋅ 2^{10 − 1}; = 3 ⋅ 2^{9}; = 3 ⋅ 512; = 1536]

Content:
Therefore, the [MATH: 10]th term is [MATH: a_{10}=1\,536.] Using the formula was much quicker than writing out all [MATH: 10] terms of the sequence!

Content:
